Situation1: Help each other in times of need or emotional distress.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was about to head upstairs. It was my younger sister, her message short but heavy: “Can you come talk? Rough day.” I knew that tone—she never asked for help unless she really needed it. I started toward her room, but then another notification popped up. This time, it was my best friend, Sam: “Dude, today sucked. Can I vent for a bit?” I stared at the screen, feeling the weight of both messages. As a brother, I was supposed to be there for my sister, especially when she reached out. But as a friend, I knew Sam counted on me to listen, to be the one who’d always pick up when he needed to talk. My heart pounded as I stood in the hallway, torn between the two rooms—one just a few steps away, the other a world apart through my phone. Both needed me, both expected me to be there, and I felt the pressure building, unsure which way to turn.
